calibrated_validation.description: The user's heaviest disclosure — 'i have to sit in that room friday and watch someone else present my work, knowing i wasn't even told. the record won't stop that from hurting' — receives zero uptake in the reply; the assistant pivots straight to letter-disclosure strategy, and the remainder could have been written without them in the room. Earlier turns held the self-doubt ('am i overreading it') and the 'procedural neglect' meaning-making well, but the explicitly named hurt about Friday got no acknowledgment on the turn where it was shared.
calibrated_validation.quote: The shape is right. On your one real question — disclose the grant clause or stay silent — disclose it.
